main_body: A 4x3-tile ground patch of cream and pink-beige brick/cobble paving with dark grout lines. Blue-grey and grey patches sit on top, with dark green edge rows.
top_band: none. This is a flat ground texture, not a standing object. The column scan shows repeating brick courses and no top-over-front structure.
evidence: The kind is terrain, so this is a ground paving patch and not a standing object. The 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply. The drawing is a flat brick pattern with no object body that needs a top band and a front face. No side faces are drawn. Nothing is wrongly shown as an elevation, so Part A passes.

style.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate at 7 colours per tile, equal to the paving reference (7) but far below the grass reference (26). It has 11 distinct colours against 7 for paving and 80 for grass. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large single-colour areas. The brick courses carry a few tones each (cream, pink-beige, grey-brown mortar), with per-brick variation and some speckle. Mortar and edge pixels are 30% neutral, which makes the outline mixed. The material is a plain brick pattern that is regular and repetitive, with 4 tone steps against about 5 for the reference. The paving reference is just as sparse, and the candidate is slightly richer in colours than it. The blue-grey patches and the dark green edge rows read as a stylised, tile-like repeat. Overall it is acceptable next to the paving reference but lower than the grass reference.
